### 6.11 Cody's Tony Chachere's Smoked Turkey

**❤️ Family favorite** — *Cody, 2026-09-09: "one of the best in the world."* And on the plan to write it up: *"I love the turkey one."*

**Cody's own turkey, dictated 2026-09-09.** The shape of it: **the night before, inject the bird with *a whole bunch* of Tony Chachere's Creole Style Butter injectable marinade, hit it *liberally* with Tony Chachere's Original Creole Seasoning, and stand it upright on a cavity stand in the fridge overnight** — *"not beer-can — a rack, a thing that goes inside its butt and it sits upright."* **It stays upright through the smoke.** The next day it goes on the Big Green Egg, **per the Egg's own published turkey method** — he forgets the temperature: *"three fifty, three seventy-five, something like that — a cross between cooking the inside and crisping the skin."* That number is filled below from the Big Green Egg's own guidance and labeled; his replaces it the day he remembers.

> 🧂 **Two products, same company — and he confirmed both by name.** *"Tony Chachere's butter injectable, and also Tony Chachere's Creole seasoning for the rub. It's the seasoning and an injection — two different products, same company."* So: **Tony Chachere's Creole Style Butter Injectable Marinade** goes *inside* the bird through a needle, and **Tony Chachere's Original Creole Seasoning** goes *on* it as the rub. Don't confuse them at the store, and don't buy one thinking it does both jobs. *(The seasoning is the green-label **Original** — not the BOLD blend [§7.9 Caveman Chicken Wings](79-caveman-chicken-wings.md) uses.)*

> ⚠️🧂 **Tony's is salted — so this is a Path B bird, and no kosher salt goes on it. Read [§6.1](61-smoked-brisket.md)'s salt-it-once warning before you reach for the salt bowl.** Tony Chachere's Creole Seasoning is a salt-forward blend, which means **the liberal coat that goes on the night before *is* the dry brine** ([§T37](t37-salt-brining-and-the-dry-brine--codys-standing-practice-heavy-every-time.md)) — the salt draws moisture out, pulls it back in seasoned, and the uncovered night in the fridge dries the skin for crisping. [§6.1 Smoked Brisket](61-smoked-brisket.md)'s rule in one line: *if your rub carries the salt, put it on the night before so the salt has time to work* — which is exactly what Cody does here — *and don't add a salt dry brine underneath it.* [§7.9](79-caveman-chicken-wings.md) runs its wings on the identical rule: *Tony's is the salt — don't add more.* **And note the injectable is a seasoned marinade too, so this bird carries salt from two Tony's products; that is his method and it is not softened here.** *(Cookbook caution, labeled: [§T80](t80-choosing-your-turkey.md) says most supermarket birds are already pumped with a salt solution — "basted," "enhanced," or kosher. On one of those, this would be a third dose. Buy an unsalted bird if you can find one; if you can't, go a shade lighter on the rub than "liberal." His method assumes the bird he buys, which isn't recorded — see Open Questions.)*

> 🌡️ **The Egg temperature — cookbook judgment under [CLAUDE.md §3d](../../CLAUDE.md), labeled, and his number supersedes it.** Cody said to cook it *per the Big Green Egg's own turkey guidance* and couldn't recall the figure — *"three fifty, three seventy-five, something like that."* **Big Green Egg's own published whole-bird *Smoked Turkey* recipe sets the Egg for indirect cooking at 325°F with the convEGGtor in**, about **12 minutes per pound**, to an internal **165°F**, with hickory or pecan as the wood; its **spatchcocked** turkey recipe runs **350°F**, which is very likely the number he half-remembers. *(The figures come by way of the Egg's own recipe pages; those pages couldn't be opened directly from this environment, so no URL is attached — the publisher and the recipe are named instead.)* **This cookbook's other turkey authority lands in the same place:** [§T81 Cooking the Perfect Turkey](t81-cooking-the-perfect-turkey.md) (Meathead) says to *roast the bird as close to 325°F as your cooker will let you — this crisps the skin*, and [§7.122](7122-the-ultimate-smoked-turkey.md) runs at 325°F. That is precisely the *"cross between cooking the inside and crisping the skin"* he described. **So the recipe below runs at 325°F.** If he lands on 350°F, use it — a whole bird is forgiving of that difference and the timing tightens a little; it's his number the day he gives it.

> 🎯 **Doneness is Cody's own standing rule, already on the record: pull at 160°F in the breast, at the very most.** He set it on [§7.122](7122-the-ultimate-smoked-turkey.md) on 2026-09-07, and it applies to every whole turkey he cooks. Big Green Egg prints 165°F; the USDA minimum and this cookbook's poultry floor ([§T44](t44-food-safety--the-real-logic-and-the-target-temperature-table.md)) are 165°F; **a whole bird pulled at 160°F carries over to that on the board** ([§T33](t33-how-meat-actually-cooks--conduction-carryover-and-why-resting-is-a-myth.md)), which is also why it gets carved straight away rather than tented. Past 160°F the breast dries out fast.

> 🦃 **Read this beside [§7.122 The Ultimate Smoked Turkey](7122-the-ultimate-smoked-turkey.md) — Meathead's bird — because they are two answers to the same holiday, and they disagree on purpose.**
>
> | | **[§6.11](611-codys-tony-chacheres-smoked-turkey.md) — Cody's** *(this one)* | **[§7.122](7122-the-ultimate-smoked-turkey.md) — Meathead's** |
> |---|---|---|

> **Where they agree is the whole of [§T81](t81-cooking-the-perfect-turkey.md):** dry brine, don't truss, nothing in the cavity, ~325°F, don't baste, pull at 160°F, don't tent, carve at once. Cody's upright stand honors two of those rules by design — see the stand note under the ingredients.

**Techniques used:** [§T37 Salt, Brining, and the Dry Brine](t37-salt-brining-and-the-dry-brine--codys-standing-practice-heavy-every-time.md) *(the overnight Tony's **is** the dry brine)* · [§T35 Smoke Science](t35-smoke-science--combustion-the-smoke-ring-and-getting-blue-smoke.md) *(blue smoke, and **Cody's palmful-of-wood rule**)* · [§T109 Indirect Heat](t109-indirect-heat--putting-something-between-the-fire-and-the-food.md) *(convEGGtor in)* · [§T80 Choosing Your Turkey](t80-choosing-your-turkey.md) · [§T81 Cooking the Perfect Turkey](t81-cooking-the-perfect-turkey.md) · [§T67 Ban the V-Shaped Rack](t67-ban-the-v-shaped-rack.md) *(why air on all sides matters — the stand's whole argument)* · [§T44 Food Safety — Target Temperatures](t44-food-safety--the-real-logic-and-the-target-temperature-table.md) · [§T82 How to Carve a Turkey](t82-how-to-carve-a-turkey.md)

**Yield:** one whole turkey — no size given; [§T80](t80-choosing-your-turkey.md)'s rule is **1 lb raw weight per person**. The figures below assume **a 14 lb bird, serving 12**, the same size [§7.122](7122-the-ultimate-smoked-turkey.md) is priced on.

**🟢 Easy** · **Prep ~45 min** *(the night before: unbagging, injecting, rubbing, and onto the stand, ~30 min; the day of: probe, wood, on and off the Egg, ~15 min)* · **Slow cook ~2½–3½ hr** *(325°F indirect on the Egg, by weight — roughly 12 minutes a pound, on the probe not the clock)* · **Start to finish ~1 day** *(includes the overnight dry brine; add 24 hr per 4 lb to thaw a frozen bird, per [§T80](t80-choosing-your-turkey.md))*

**⏰ Countdown to dinner:** T−1 day (the night before; thaw a frozen bird first, 24 hr per 4 lb) unbag, giblets out, pat dry; inject a whole bunch of the Creole Butter all over; Tony's Original liberally, no salt; onto the stand upright, uncovered in the fridge overnight · T−3¼ to 4¼ hr light the Egg, 325°F indirect, convEGGtor in, drip pan, a palmful of pecan or hickory, wait for blue smoke and let it settle · T−2¾ to 3¾ hr bird on its stand, probe in the breast, dome down and left alone — about 12 min a pound (~2 hr 50 min for 14 lb) · T−15 min off at 160°F in the breast, at the very most; off the stand, carve right away, no tent · T−0 board juices spooned over.

> **Why 🟢 Easy — and why [§7.122](7122-the-ultimate-smoked-turkey.md) is 🟡 and this isn't.** [CLAUDE.md §3a](../../CLAUDE.md)'s test: *can a step go from perfect to ruined?* Walk it. Injecting can't fail. Rubbing can't fail. A night on a stand in the fridge can't fail. Bringing an Egg to 325°F and waiting for blue smoke can't fail. **The one thing that can go wrong with a turkey — overshooting the breast — is a pull-at-a-number, not a technique**, and with a leave-in probe and his 160°F rule it's the same kind of step as [§6.1](61-smoked-brisket.md)'s 165°F wrap point, which is 🟢. [§7.122](7122-the-ultimate-smoked-turkey.md) earned its 🟡 for two things this recipe doesn't have: a pan-drippings gravy that can scorch, and a mid-cook handoff of a screaming-hot 15-pound bird off the grate and back on. **Here the bird goes on once, stays on its stand, and comes off once.** The hours in between are the Egg's, and per [§1 Cody's Pho](1-codys-pho.md) hours never inflate a rating. *(The prep figure is the cookbook's — he gave no time for this bird; his figure for the Meathead one was 45.)*

#### A. Ingredients

- **1 whole turkey** — **thawed all the way through** *(no size given — see Open Questions; [§T80](t80-choosing-your-turkey.md): 1 lb per person, 24 hr in the fridge per 4 lb to thaw, and **two small birds beat one giant one**. The figures here assume 14 lb)*
- **Tony Chachere's Creole Style Butter Injectable Marinade** — ✅ ***"a whole bunch."*** **That is Cody's amount and it is also the manufacturer's** — Tony's own turkey directions say to *use as much as you'd like* and to *space out the injection sites so the marinade goes throughout the entire turkey.* Figure a bottle for a bird *(what's actually left in the meat is estimated in the Nutrition block)*
- **Tony Chachere's Original Creole Seasoning** — ✅ ***liberally*** — every surface, and inside the cavity. **This is the salt. No kosher salt goes on this bird** — see the warning above
- **Smoking wood — a palmful, and no more** *(his standing rule, [§T35](t35-smoke-science--combustion-the-smoke-ring-and-getting-blue-smoke.md). **He didn't say which wood for the turkey** — see Open Questions. The Egg's own recipe names **hickory or pecan**; **pecan** is his favorite everywhere else in this book — [§6.1](61-smoked-brisket.md), [§6.9](69-codys-pulled-pork.md), [§6.10](610-sous-vide-brisket-richies-method.md))*

*Not groceries, but the recipe doesn't happen without them — and per [CLAUDE.md §3e](../../CLAUDE.md), the two Tony's products and the stand are all orderable online if the store is out:* **an upright turkey stand** *(a cavity stand — the cone or frame that goes up inside the bird so it sits upright, the kind sold as a vertical turkey roaster; **"not beer-can,"** in his words — nothing goes in the cavity but the stand)*, **a marinade injector** *(the syringe; buy one if the bottle you find doesn't come with one)*, a **Big Green Egg or kamado with the convEGGtor**, a **drip pan**, a **sheet pan** for the fridge, and a **leave-in probe thermometer**.

> 🧍 **Why the upright stand is a good idea and not just a quirk** *(cookbook reasoning, labeled — Cody said only that this is how he does it)*. Two of [§T81](t81-cooking-the-perfect-turkey.md)'s rules are built into it. **"Never put the turkey in a roasting pan"** — a pan blocks airflow and leaves the underside soggy; [§T67](t67-ban-the-v-shaped-rack.md) shows that meat needs hot air on **every side** to cook evenly. A bird standing on a cavity stand has air on every side by definition, underside included. **"Do not put anything in the cavity"** — leave it open so heat and smoke can get in. **An upright bird's cavity is open at the bottom, straight over the heat**, so the inside cooks along with the outside instead of lagging behind it; that's the *"cooking the inside"* half of his own description. And the skin gets the same dry, all-around heat everywhere, which is the *"crisping the skin"* half. It also does the overnight job well: standing on a sheet pan, uncovered, every inch of skin is in the fridge air. **The one thing a stand can't help with is the dome** — see Open Questions on whether a big bird fits upright in his Egg.

#### B. Cooking Instructions

**1. The night before — unbag the bird, giblets out, and pat it dry.**
Neck and giblets out of both cavities, any pop-up timer out and thrown away *(they're wrong — [§T81](t81-cooking-the-perfect-turkey.md))*, and **pat the whole bird dry, inside and out, with paper towels** — the rub sticks to dry skin and slides off wet skin. *(The drying is the cookbook's gloss, not his instruction; the rest of this step is the same start every whole bird in this book gets.)* If the drumsticks are tied together, cut the tie: **don't truss it** — [§T81](t81-cooking-the-perfect-turkey.md)'s rule, and on a stand the legs hang free anyway.

**2. Inject it — "a whole bunch" of the Creole Butter marinade, all over the bird.**
✅ **Cody's amount, and Tony's own direction:** *use as much as you'd like, and space out the injection sites so the marinade goes throughout the entire turkey.* **Shake the bottle hard first** — it's a butter-flavored emulsion and it separates in the bottle. Then work around the bird: **both breasts, several sites each, in from the side and from the top; both thighs; both drumsticks.** Small doses at many sites beat a flood at one — push the needle in, pull it back a little as you press the plunger so the marinade spreads along the needle track, and move on. **Some of it will run back out. That's normal; keep going.** *(The site-by-site technique is cookbook gloss; the amount and the product are his.)* This is also, for the record, the one place in this book where Cody and [§T81](t81-cooking-the-perfect-turkey.md)'s *don't hide the bird under powerful injections* part ways — and it is his bird, his call, and *"one of the best in the world."*

**3. Hit it liberally with Tony's Original Creole Seasoning. Every surface, into the cavity. No salt.**
✅ **Cody's word is *liberally*, and he means it.** Every surface — breast, back, legs, wings, under the wings, and a shake inside the cavity. **This is the dry brine** ([§T37](t37-salt-brining-and-the-dry-brine--codys-standing-practice-heavy-every-time.md)): Tony's is salt-forward, the salt goes in overnight, and the seasoning goes in with it. **No kosher salt. Nothing else.** *(Path B, per [§6.1](61-smoked-brisket.md) — the salted rub the night before **instead of** a plain-salt brine, never on top of one.)*

**4. Onto the stand, upright, and into the fridge uncovered. Overnight.**
Set the stand on a sheet pan, **lower the bird onto it so the stand goes up into the cavity and the bird sits upright** — *"a thing that goes inside its butt and it sits upright"* — and put the whole pan in the refrigerator, **uncovered, overnight.** Two things happen while you sleep, and they're why the night matters: the salt in the rub travels in, and the open fridge air dries the skin so it can crisp instead of steam — exactly [§7.9](79-caveman-chicken-wings.md)'s reasoning for its own overnight Tony's. *(Time not stated beyond "overnight" — [§T37](t37-salt-brining-and-the-dry-brine--codys-standing-practice-heavy-every-time.md)'s range for turkey is at least 2–4 hours and [§7.122](7122-the-ultimate-smoked-turkey.md)'s is 12–24; overnight sits comfortably inside both.)*

**5. Next day — the Egg to 325°F, indirect, a palmful of wood, and wait for blue smoke.**
**325°F** ⚙️ *(cookbook fill from Big Green Egg's own whole-bird recipe — see the temperature note above; his figure supersedes it)*, **convEGGtor in** for indirect heat ([§T109](t109-indirect-heat--putting-something-between-the-fire-and-the-food.md)), and **a drip pan on the convEGGtor** under where the bird will stand — the fat that comes off a butter-injected bird is considerable, and it's better in a pan than on the ceramic *(the pan is a cookbook suggestion; there's no gravy made from it here)*. **A palmful of wood and no more** — his standing rule at [§T35](t35-smoke-science--combustion-the-smoke-ring-and-getting-blue-smoke.md), and a turkey is a mild meat that takes smoke fast. **Then wait for the smoke to go thin and blue** before the bird goes anywhere near it — the first, white smoke is the bitter stuff, and it burns off; [§6.1](61-smoked-brisket.md) step 4 has the full version of this rule. Give a ceramic cooker time to settle at the number, not just touch it.

**6. Bird on, still on its stand. Probe in the breast. Close the dome and leave it alone.**
Lift the bird **on its stand** straight from the sheet pan onto the grate, over the drip pan. **A leave-in probe into the thickest part of the breast**, a little past dead center and not touching bone — this recipe is run on that number. Then close the dome and **don't open it**: no basting *(it softens the skin — [§T81](t81-cooking-the-perfect-turkey.md))*, no peeking. **Figure roughly 12 minutes a pound at 325°F** — about **2 hr 50 min for a 14 lb bird** — but that's a planning number, not a pull time; [§7.122](7122-the-ultimate-smoked-turkey.md)'s table under its step 8 gives the same range by weight. *(Cookbook observation, labeled: standing upright, the thighs and drumsticks sit lowest and nearest the heat and the breast highest and farthest from it — the right way round, since dark meat wants to finish hotter than breast.)*

**7. Pull it at 160°F in the breast — at the very most.**
✅ **Cody's rule**, set on [§7.122](7122-the-ultimate-smoked-turkey.md): **160°F in the breast, and not past it.** Carryover takes a whole bird the rest of the way to the 165°F floor ([§T44](t44-food-safety--the-real-logic-and-the-target-temperature-table.md)) while it comes off and gets carved. Check a thigh too — it should read higher, and on an upright bird it will.

**8. Off the Egg, off the stand, and carve it right away. Don't tent it.**
**The stand and the bird together are heavy and very hot** — two hands in thick gloves, or two people, and go straight to a board with a channel *(the Bear Paws trick at [§7.122](7122-the-ultimate-smoked-turkey.md) step 11 works here too)*. Slide the bird off the stand onto the board. **Then carve — now.** [§T81](t81-cooking-the-perfect-turkey.md): *do not rest or tent with foil* — steam under foil softens the skin you just spent a night and three hours crisping, and the resting-redistributes-juices idea is a myth ([§T33](t33-how-meat-actually-cooks--conduction-carryover-and-why-resting-is-a-myth.md)). [§T82](t82-how-to-carve-a-turkey.md) has the carving. **Whatever collects on the board and in the drip pan is Creole butter and turkey — spoon it over the slices.** *(That last line is the cookbook's suggestion, not his.)*

#### C. Grocery Shopping List

**🛒 General grocery**

- 🛒 **Whole turkey** — size not given; **1 lb per person**, and an **unsalted** bird if you can find one *(see the warning above and [§T80](t80-choosing-your-turkey.md))*
- 🛒 **Tony Chachere's Creole Style Butter Injectable Marinade** — 1 bottle *(the injectable — in the marinade aisle or with the Cajun seasonings; **orderable online**)*
- 🛒 **Tony Chachere's Original Creole Seasoning** — a large shaker; the green-label **Original** *(this is the salt — buy nothing else to salt it with)*
- 🛒 Smoking wood — **a palmful is the whole amount**; pecan or hickory *(his wood for the turkey isn't recorded — see Open Questions)*
- 🛒 Paper towels, and a disposable foil drip pan

**🧰 Equipment — buy once, and orderable online per [CLAUDE.md §3e](../../CLAUDE.md)**

- 🧰 **Upright turkey stand** — a cavity stand / vertical turkey roaster; **not a beer-can rig**
- 🧰 **Marinade injector** — if the bottle you find doesn't come with one
- 🧰 Leave-in probe thermometer

#### Nutrition *(estimated — on an assumed 14 lb bird and an assumed amount of injection, both labeled)*

**No size and no measured injection were given** — *"a whole bunch."* The block runs on a **14 lb turkey**, the same assumption as [§7.122](7122-the-ultimate-smoked-turkey.md), and on **about 1 cup of the Creole Butter marinade actually staying in the meat** *(more goes in; some runs out at the needle holes and more drips off in the cook)*. **The marinade's own label figures aren't on record here** — it's estimated as a seasoned, butter-flavored oil emulsion at roughly 30 calories and 3 g of fat an ounce, which is the kind of product it is. The seasoning adds no calories. Scale linearly for a different bird. *(Estimated per [CLAUDE.md §3b](../../CLAUDE.md).)*

| | Calories | Fat | Protein | Carbs | Fiber |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Whole dish** *(a 14 lb bird, as eaten, plus ~1 cup of injection retained)* | ~10,200 | 565 g | 1,030 g | 8 g | 0 g |
| **Per serving** *(serves 12, holiday portions)* | ~850 | 47 g | 86 g | 1 g | 0 g |

**What a serving is:** about **8 oz of sliced turkey, mixed light and dark meat** — a holiday plate's worth, with a spoon of the board juices over it.

**The number that actually moves here is sodium, which these blocks don't track:** a liberal coat of a salt-forward seasoning on top of a salted marinade, on a bird that may have been salted by the processor too. That's the reason for the salt warning at the top, not a reason to change the recipe.

#### D. Open Questions

- ⚙️ **The Egg temperature is cookbook judgment — 325°F from Big Green Egg's own whole-bird recipe, agreeing with [§T81](t81-cooking-the-perfect-turkey.md).** He said *"three fifty, three seventy-five, something like that."* If he confirms 350°F — the Egg's own number for a spatchcocked bird — the recipe runs at 350°F and this note closes. **His figure supersedes.**
- ❓ **Which Egg, and does the bird fit upright under the dome?** A 14 lb turkey standing on a cavity stand is tall. Whether he cooks on a Large or an XL, whether he uses a raised grid or the standard one, and how big a bird he's stood up this way are all unrecorded — and they decide whether this method has a size limit.
- ❓ **How much of the injectable actually goes in — a bottle? Half?** *"A whole bunch"* is his amount and Tony's own direction is *as much as you'd like*, so the recipe is honest as written; a figure would tighten the Nutrition block, which assumes about a cup retained.
- ❓ **What wood, and does he use any?** Not stated. Pecan is his favorite across this book; the Egg's recipe names hickory or pecan. Written as *a palmful of pecan or hickory* with the palmful being the only firm part.
- ❓ **What size bird, and does he buy an unsalted one?** [§T80](t80-choosing-your-turkey.md) says most supermarket birds are pumped with salt; this method puts two salted products on top of whatever the bird came with. Whether he seeks out an unsalted bird, or just cooks the one from the store, changes how "liberal" the rub should be.
- ⚙️ **The 160°F pull is his rule from [§7.122](7122-the-ultimate-smoked-turkey.md), applied here as his standing turkey rule.** He didn't restate it for this bird; if he pulls this one differently, it goes here.
- ❓ **Anything on the wing tips?** [§7.122](7122-the-ultimate-smoked-turkey.md) foils the wing tips and drumstick ends so they don't burn. He didn't mention it; not added.
